candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite mixed numbers and/or whole numbers as equivalent fractions (often improper, or with a specified denominator) to enable fraction operations.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S01 and C:S01 explicitly include converting mixed numbers to improper fractions and rewriting integers as fractions; B separates this into its own skill (B:S02) focused on mixed-to-improper conversion, which is the closest match to the mixed/whole-to-fraction concept.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common (often least common) denominator and convert each fraction to an equivalent fraction with that denominator.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A:S02 and C:S02 directly name common-denominator selection and conversion; B:S01 covers creating equivalent fractions with a specified denominator (including scaling numerator/denominator), which operationally serves the same role as common-denominator conversion in subtraction workflows.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Compute the difference of two rational numbers once they are in compatible form (e.g., same denominator or separated whole and fractional parts).
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks include an identically scoped subtraction skill: perform the subtraction after denominators are aligned or after decomposing mixed numbers into whole/fractional parts.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Express the computed result in simplest accepted form by reducing fractions and/or converting between improper fractions, mixed numbers, and integers.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three codebooks define the same post-computation skill: reduce to lowest terms and present as integer/mixed number when appropriate.

alignment_summary: All skill_ids from A, B, and C align into four shared concepts with full 3/3 consensus. The only naming/granularity difference is that Expert B separates mixed-to-improper conversion (B:S02) from equivalent-fraction scaling to a target denominator (B:S01), whereas Experts A and C bundle whole/mixed-to-fraction conversion together and treat common-denominator conversion as its own skill.
